device.name: RIGOL DG4202 signal source (WaveBench dg4202 driver)

facts.text: The DG4000 driver accepts the models DG4062, DG4102, DG4162 and DG4202, and it accepts configuration writes only on a DG4202
The generator has two output channels, 1 and 2
The identity query *IDN? is parsed into four comma-separated fields (manufacturer, model, serial number, firmware) and the manufacturer must be RIGOL TECHNOLOGIES

A status snapshot reads the output state, the function, the frequency, the amplitude, the amplitude unit, the offset, the phase, the frequency mode, the sweep state, the APPLy response and the square-wave duty cycle
An output is switched with ':OUTP<channel> ON' or ':OUTP<channel> OFF' and read back with ':OUTP<channel>?'
A frequency is written as ':SOUR<channel>:FREQ <value>' after the frequency mode is switched to FIX when it is not FIX
A function is written as ':SOUR<channel>:FUNC <FUNCTION>' with the canonical names SIN, SQU, RAMP, PULS, NOIS and DC (aliases such as SINE, SQUARE or TRI are accepted and normalized)
An amplitude is written in Vpp: the driver first writes ':SOUR<channel>:VOLT:UNIT VPP', then ':SOUR<channel>:VOLT <value>'
A square-wave duty cycle is written as ':SOUR<channel>:FUNC:SQU:DCYC <percent>' and read back with the same command followed by '?'
The class refuses a frequency that is not > 0 Hz
The class refuses an amplitude that is not > 0 V
The class refuses a square-wave duty cycle that is not strictly between 0 and 100 percent
A failed output transaction is recovered by forcing that channel OFF before the error is raised
The clone leaves the source amplitude ceiling to the operator: SafetyLimitsConfig.max_source_vpp defaults to None
Setting a voltage, an amplitude or a frequency never switches an output on by itself
